Form 7 is used to seek the deletion of a person’s name from the electoral rolls if they are deceased, have shifted elsewhere or have two voter IDs. The forms submitted by Balachander contain the names of Muslim residents from the same slum in Chikkadapally. They’re all his neighbours. None of the 30 names Balachander has submitted meet the criteria for deletion. Congress BLA and the party’s Bhaglingampally division vice president Mohammad Baba Sharfuddin is also among the 30 names Balachander submitted for deletion. He lives a mere 150 metres away from Balachander’s residence and has known the BJP BLA for over two decades. “I have been a BLA in this area for nearly 20 years. I got a call from the BLO a week ago saying that form 7 was submitted seeking my deletion. I was baffled,” Sharfuddin told TNM . “I then learnt that it wasn’t just my name but also my wife’s, my four siblings and their wives and some of their children. A total of twenty names from my family alone were submitted for deletion,” he added. After learning this, Sharfuddin confronted Balachander. “I asked him how he could do this. But he just told me that they had given him the forms in the BJP office and asked him to submit them. He said, ‘Anna (elder brother), I don’t know what Form 7 is used for,’” Sharfuddin said. TNM made multiple phone calls to Balachander and even visited his house, but he remained unreachable. The allegations aren’t limited to Sharfuddin and his family. A stone’s throw away from Balachander’s home lives Shareef. Ten of his family members are also among the names Balachander submitted. “I only learnt of the issue when officials came for an enquiry,” Shareef’s brother Nawaz told TNM. Sharfuddin informed election officials, including the constituency’s Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) Praveen Reddy. A first enquiry was conducted by the BLO and lower officials, while a second was carried out by the ER

याचिका को खारिज किया, दिल्ली दंगा केस में उमर खालिद-शरजील इमाम को की जमानत याचिका फिर खारिज, संभल-हिंसा के मुख्य आरोपी मुल्ला अफरोज पर लगा NSA रद्द, मामले में सुप्रीम कोर्ट की योगी सरकार पर कड़ी items.title: IIULER student Advika Gupta wins 5 gold medals at Commonwealth Powerlifting Championships in Canada
items.summary: Advika Gupta , a second-year B.A. LL.B. student at the India International University of Legal Education and Research (IIULER), Goa, has won 5 gold medals at the Commonwealth Powerlifting Championships held in Canada. Advika won the medals in the women’s sub-junior category in the under-63 kg weight class. She won the Overall, Squat, Bench Press, Deadlift and Single-Lift Bench Press categories. She was also awarded the Best Lifter title in Bench Press. In a press release, IIULER Vice-Chancellor (VC) R Ventaka Rao said that Advika competing at such a prestigious international championship while pursuing her academic responsibilities is a remarkable accomplishment. “Her success is a proud moment for her family, the institution and the nation. Excelling across multiple events demonstrates a high level of preparation, determination and sporting spirit. IIULER is proud to have supported her with the encouragement and opportunities necessary to excel both academically and beyond the classroom,” Dr. Rao added. items.title: Youth Congress moves Delhi High Court against denial of permission to protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar
items.summary: The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) has moved the Delhi High Court challenging the Delhi Police's refusal to permit them to hold a demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar. The plea has been filed by IYC national president Uday Bhanu Chib and is likely to be heard by the High Court next week. Chib has challenged the Delhi Police’s order of October 1 rejecting their application. According to the plea, the IYC had applied on September 25 seeking permission to hold a peaceful demonstration involving around 100-150 people. The organisation said it had undertaken to comply with all lawful conditions relating to security, traffic management, discipline and maintenance of public order. The plea states that despite repeated follow-ups, the police communicated the rejection only on October 1, which was also the first proposed date of the demonstration. The petition contends that the police's power to regulate assemblies does not extend to imposing a blanket prohibition without an individualised and proportionate assessment of the circumstances. It states that the police’s decision amounts to a violation of fundamental rights to freedom of speech and expression and peaceful assembly under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution. The plea also challenges the "mechanical application" of guidelines governing protests and assemblies. The plea has been filed through advocate Roopesh Singh Bhadauria.

items.title: Karnataka High Court grants bail to man accused of tampering with forensic lab report
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently granted bail to a man accused of tampering with a Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) report in a case registered over the alleged murder of an ex-army officer [ Kumar @ Dali v State of Karnataka ]. The case involves allegations that the deceased ex-army man's wife (accused no.1) plotted to murder him along with her alleged paramour (accused no.2) to claim insurance money. The bail applicant (accused no. 10), Kumar, was accused of tampering with a report on the forensic evidence of the crime to help the prime accused after he was paid a bribe. On September 30, Justice Venkatesh Naik T granted Kumar bail after noting his alleged role in the crime was confined to him allegedly issuing a tampered forensic report to mask the evidence. "Whether petitioner/accused No.10 assisted in tempering with the report issued by the government scientific agency is a matter of trial and the same has to be established during the course of the evidence. The petitioner is a permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause title of the petition and he is ready and willing to abide by the conditions to be imposed by this Court. Under these circumstances, this court is of the opinion that the petitioner may be enlarged on bail with stringent conditions," the Court added. Justice Venkatesh Naik T The murder case involves allegations that the deceased's wife took advantage of her husband's alcoholism to murder him and claim an insurance policy taken in his name by forging his signature. She allegedly got her husband drunk and allowed him to drive a car so that he met with an accident, paving way for the wife to claim the insurance policy taken in his name. Although the husband met with an accident, he survived and suffered minor injuries. He was admitted to a hospital. The wife's paramour is then alleged to have administered sleeping pills and poisonous substances via saline, which led to the husband's death at the hospital. A postmortem exam was eventually conducted. The deceased's wife is alleged to have bribed a Regional Forensic Science Laboratory (RFSL) Officer to prepare a report which said that her husband was sober before his death, and that his body did not contain any poison. The wife's paramour, however, later approached the police and made a confession about his involvement in the alleged murder. He also spoke about the involvement of nine people in the crime, including the deceased man's wife. In total, ten persons were arraigned

items.title: 30-year-old NOIDA housing dispute: Supreme Court appoints former judge to identify genuine allottees
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently constituted a one-member high-powered independent committee headed by former Allahabad High Court Justice Sudhir Kumar Saxena to finalise the list of genuine members and subsequent purchasers entitled to multi-storeyed flats in NOIDA [ New Okhla Industrial Development Authority v. items.title: Plea in Delhi High Court challenges appointment of additional public prosecutors on deputation, short-term contracts
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently issued notice to the Delhi government on a public interest litigation (PIL) challenging a notification allowing the recruitment of additional public prosecutors (APPs) through deputation and short-term contractual engagement from outside the regular prosecutorial cadre [Shipra Mishra v. Govt of NCT of Delhi] . A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said that the reply should be filed in two weeks. The Court will hear the matter next on November 4. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia The petition, filed by Advocate Shipra Mishra, challenges the notification dated April 2, 2026, which provides for filling APP posts through 85% promotion and 15% deputation/contractual engagement. Mishra argues that the 15% quota violates Section 18(6) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. According to the plea, Section 18(6) requires public prosecutors and APPs to be appointed from the regular prosecuting officers' cadre - where such a cadre exists - except when suitable candidates are unavailable. The petitioner claims that Delhi has a functional prosecutorial cadre comprising eligible APPs and that the notification does not record any finding that suitable cadre officers are unavailable. Therefore, it alleged that the notification creates a parallel route of entry into the prosecutorial service. "The impugned action is further arbitrary, unreasonable, and violative of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India," the plea states. It adds that the device of “short-term contractual engagement” is a mechanism to circumvent the legislative mandate embodied in Section 18(6) BNSS. "The arbitrary induction of deputationists unfamiliar with local court practices and prosecutorial procedures is likely to result in inefficiency, delay, and procedural irregularities, thereby prejudicing the rights of victims and eroding public confidence in the justice," the plea adds. Advocates Dr Hemant Gupta, Rony John and Akash Aggarwal appeared for the petitioner. Advocates Avnish Ahlawat, Tania Ahlawat, Nitesh Kumar Singh, Aliza Alam and Mohnish Sehrawat represented the Delhi government. items.title: A decade of judicial vacancies: Who is responsible for filling the gap?
items.summary: The Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court recently noted that an affidavit filed by Maharashtra's Law and Judiciary Department showed that nearly 60% of judicial posts in the State are vacant. The judge reportedly called such a shortage "glaring" and made a call for urgent steps to fill the vacancies. What is more glaring, however, is how little has changed in judicial vacancies over the last decade. There can be many reasons behind the high level of vacancies, ranging from supply-side factors - such as a lack of well-qualified candidates or an inability to acquire and retain them - to demand-side factors, such as budgetary constraints, lack of infrastructure to support an increased number of judges, or failures in ensuring timely appointment cycles. In any case, what we need is sustained attention to the issue. Appointments to the district judiciary are made by state governments (through the support of public service commissions) and High Courts to vacant positions in the sanctioned strength of judges. Without going into the age-old issue of the method to be used to calculate judge strength and the merits of each method proposed in the past, appointing authorities known one thing - a sanctioned strength of judges in each state which can be filled. items.title: Madras High Court refuses to recall order to disclose microplastics in packaged water, sugar, salt
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently refused to recall an interim order directing the addition of labels to bottled drinking water and packaged salt and sugar to disclose that such products may contain microplastics [ FSSAI Vs PET ]. A Bench of Justices N Sathish Kumar and D Bharatha Chakravarthy rejected a review petition filed by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) and recall applications filed by industry bodies against the February 6 interim order directing that such products to carry warning labels. The Court rejected arguments that the introduction of such mandatory disclosure labels should be put off until the FSSAI completes its assessment of the actual risk posed by microplastics to human beings. The Court held that a disclosure that bottled water and packaged sugar or salt "may" contain microplastics is a bare minimum measure to help consumers make informed choices. "The order dated 06.02.2026, without causing any aspersions on safety or causing the least alarm, ordered only the barest essential minimum, namely informing the consumer that the food may contain micro/nano plastics... the review/recall petitioners' contention as to how far human beings can withstand and tolerate micro/nano plastic particles should be first determined becomes redundant... we see no reason or ground to review or recall the order dated 06.02.2026," the Court said. Justice N Sathish Kumar and Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy The Court passed the order after noting that the FSSAI, the PET Packaging Association for Clean Environment (PACE) and the Federation of All India Packaged Drinking Water Manufacturers Associations did not dispute the presence of micro or nano plastics in packaged water, sugar or salt. “ If something is present inside, it would be mandatory to disclose it on the label. The core principle behind levelling [labelling] is disclosure of information/truth," the Court held. The Bench was particularly critical of the argument that such warnings could adversely affect businesses. “ The arguments require sweeping inconvenient facts under the carpet because of a perceived commercial backlash," it said. In February, the High Court had directed that plastic or PET bottles selling water should carry, in at least font size 10 and bold red letters, the statement, “ This water may contain Micro/Nano Plastics. ” Sugar and salt sold in plastic packaging were similarly required to carry warnings that they may contain micro or nano plastics. items.title: Is slipping into DMs enough to prove adultery by wife? Allahabad High Court answers
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently said that a husband cannot merely rely on social media messages to establish that his wife is continuously “living in adultery” without corroborative evidence of physical intimacy or cohabitation. Justice Jai Krishna Upadhyay was dealing with a husband’s plea challenging the grant of maintenance to his wife. The husband’s primary argument was that his wife was disentitled from claiming any maintenance as she is “living in adultery”. In this regard, he placed reliance on printouts of Instagram chats alleged to have taken place between her and an advocate, with whom she is allegedly in an adulterous relationship. However, the Court said that the husband has to prove a continuous “adulterous lifestyle” of his wife to deny maintenance to her. It said that Instagram chats were not sufficient to establish the alleged adultery. “Even if, for the sake of argument, the contents of the unverified chats were to be perused, mere text messages on a social media platform, without corroborative evidence of physical intimacy or cohabitation, are thoroughly insufficient to legally establish that the wife is continuously "living in adultery",” the Court said. It explained that “living in adultery” – a ground for denying maintenance to a wife under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) or Section 144 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) – denotes a continuous, ongoing and habitual course of adulterous conduct. “It does not encompass a single, fleeting lapse, nor can it be inferred from mere conversational interactions, professional associations, or unsubstantiated suspicions. For a husband to successfully non-suit a wife's claim for maintenance at the threshold, he must present clear and cogent evidence,” the Court added. It also observed that electronic evidence requires strict verification in accordance with Section 65-B of the Indian Evidence Act due to the inherent vulnerabilities of digital data. In the present case, it said, the husband had not produced the mandatory statutory certification. Having found that the messages exchanged on Instagram were not sufficient to establish the accusation of “living in adultery”, the Court dismissed the husband’s challenge against a family court order directing him to pay maintenance to his wife. items.title: Body-shaming, verbal abuse not enough to prove offence of insulting woman’s modesty: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that allegations of body-shaming and verbally abusing another woman do not, by themselves, constitute the offence of insulting a woman’s modesty under Section 509 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). Section 509 IPC criminalises words, sounds, gestures or acts intended to insult a woman’s modesty, as well as intrusions into her privacy. The provision prescribes a maximum sentence of 3 years’ imprisonment and a fine. Justice SR Krishna Kumar quashed criminal proceedings against two women, aged 25 and 27, accused of body-shaming and verbally abusing another woman in Bengaluru. “Having regard to the mandatory ingredients required to constitute an offence under Section 509 IPC, merely because the petitioners and accused No.3 (the women accused of body-shaming) are said to have bodyshamed the complainant and insulted her about her physical appearance, it cannot be said that the material on record discloses the commission of the offence punishable under Section 509 IPC,” the Court said. Justice SR Krishna Kumar The case arose from a complaint filed in August 2023 by a 26-year-old woman, who alleged that two women and a man verbally abused her and her friends the previous night. She alleged that the group used fat-shaming, body-shaming, racist and vulgar language, causing her and her friend mental trauma and distress. Based on the complaint, the police registered a First Information Report (FIR) under Section 509 of the IPC. After investigating the complaint, the police filed a chargesheet, leading to criminal proceedings before a Bengaluru magistrate court. It noted that proceedings against the third person accused in the same incident had already been quashed by the High Court in June 2024. Since the allegations against the two women were identical to those against the third accused, the Court applied the principle of parity. It held that people facing the same allegations in the same circumstances should ordinarily receive similar treatment. Advocate Ankur Trripati appeared for the petitioners. items.title: To be or not to be? Supreme Court between foundational doctrine and ad-hoc expediency
items.summary: Bar & Bench recently reported a case before the Supreme Court. The facts, simply put, are as follows: a private university encroached upon government land in Tamil Nadu, which had been allotted to the State Prison Department for an open prison. The Madras High Court ordered eviction of the private university from the encroached land. The private university has challenged the said order before the Supreme Court. During the course of the hearing, the Court suggested the State government should avoid demolishing the private university buildings and repossessing the land. Instead, it suggested that the private university should: (i) identify and provide suitable land (ii) bear the cost of purchasing land identified by the government or (iii) should pay the market price (or more than that) to the government for the land that they encroached. The Supreme Court mentioned that they are concerned because the State repossessing the land will result in the demolition of an education institution. The Court further said that if it were a commercial establishment, there would not have been any such leniency shown. This piece traverses the various theoretical bases of this suggestion made by the Supreme Court. Even though the Aristotelian concept of corrective justice in its true essence is impracticable, when modern restorative justice is put together with compensatory equity, the suggestion is a balanced one. The encroacher is made to bear the cost of the illegal possession and the larger public interest evinced by the State is protected. The harshness of demolition is a wasted remedy compared with the exemplary cost imposed on the encroacher. The suggestion by the Court yields a positive nod from the perspective of sociological jurisprudence of Roscoe Pound too, which believes in balancing of interests with minimum friction. items.title: Wife's inability to conceive not ground to grant divorce for cruelty: Madras High Court
items.summary: Childlessness cannot by itself amount to cruelty and a wife cannot be blamed merely because a married couple is unable to conceive, the Madras High Court recently observed. A Division Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi said that the inability of spouse to have a child cannot be converted into a matrimonial fault of the wife. “ Marriage cannot be reduced to the sole object of procreation. A spouse cannot be treated as having failed in the matrimonial relationship merely because the parties did not have a child, ” the Court said. Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi The Court made the observations while dismissing an appeal filed by a husband seeking divorce on the ground of cruelty. A family court had earlier dismissed the plea, prompting him to approach the High Court. The couple married in June 2007. The husband alleged that after an initially peaceful marriage, his wife began humiliating him, suspected him whenever he returned late from work, frequently left the matrimonial home and refused matrimonial companionship. He also alleged that in June 2016, she publicly called him impotent, assaulted him with footwear and later with a broom, removed her thali, tore their photographs and left the matrimonial home. The wife denied the allegations. She said she had undergone surgery for a uterine fibroid and treatment in the hope of conceiving and continuing her matrimonial life. items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Thursday held that the disciplinary committee of a State Bar Council cannot suspend a lawyer at an interim stage of disciplinary proceedings against him [Akhilesh Jaiswal and Another v Bar Council of India and 2 Others] A division bench of Justice Shekhar B Saraf and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary said the order of suspension under Section 35 (3) of the Advocates, 1961, is a final order and cannot be passed at an interim stage. “According to this Court, the order of suspension as mentioned in Section 35 (3) (c) of the Advocates Act, 1961 is a final order and could not be passed at an interim stage by the Bar Council of Uttar Pradesh,” the Court said. Justices Shekhar B Saraf and Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary The Court was dealing with a petition moved by two Lucknow lawyers challenging the license suspension of Akhilesh Jasiwal, President of Central Bar Association, Civil Court Lucknow and Avnish Dixit, Secretary of the Bar Association, during the pendency of a proceeding against them before the disciplinary committee of Bar Council of Uttar Pradesh. The Bench noted that the disciplinary committee's order dated September 26 against Jaiswal and Dixit failed to mention whether a copy of the complaint was provided to them as was requested by them. It added that while the order adjourned the hearing to October 11, it simultaneously proceeded to suspend the lawyers’ license till further orders. The Court said that the indefinite suspension of license appeared to be unsustainable in law. In this regard, it also referred to a Madras High Court ruling which said the Bar Council of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry cannot place a person under interim suspension pending disciplinary inquiry. “Upon perusal of the aforesaid judgment, it is evident that the procedure adopted by the authorities in the present case is not in consonance with the provisions of the Advocates Act, 1961,” the Court said. Accordingly, the Court quashed the suspension order. However, it asked the petitioners to appear before the State Bar Council on the next date of hearing set by the disciplinary committee. “In the event that any documents are required to be furnished to the petitioners and have not yet been supplied, the same shall be provided by the Bar Council of Uttar Pradesh, in accordance with law, upon a request being made by the petitioners within 24 hours. items.title: One Nation, One Election: Supreme Court says no parliamentary panel meeting with CJI, judges
items.summary: The Supreme Court of India has said that no meeting will take place between its judges and the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) examining the 'One Nation, One Election' bills. According to PTI , the JPC dropped the plan to meet top court judges after the opposition raised objections to the same. Earlier, Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal had revealed at a press conference that the JPC was scheduled to hold discussions with the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and other apex court judges on October 6. The JPC, chaired by BJP Member of Parliament PP Chaudhary, is examining the Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024. The two bills seek to put in place a framework for holding Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections together. Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal Sibal termed the proposed interaction unprecedented and unconstitutional. He said that a parliamentary committee briefing sitting judges on a bill, even before finalising its report, has never happened in India's history. He added that this goes against the principle of separation of powers among the executive, the legislature and the judiciary. Parliament makes laws and the judiciary tests their validity, he pointed out. If the amendments are passed, the same judges could be called upon to decide challenges to them. "This is a joke on the Constitution," Sibal said. The JPC has so far held consultations with political parties, legislators, constitutional experts and other stakeholders. It disclosed that it also consulted former Chief Justices of India and retired Supreme Court judges on the constitutional implications of simultaneous elections. Sibal's objection, however, was to an interaction with sitting judges, who could eventually sit in judgment over the constitutionality of the law. The bills require amendments to the Constitution and have sparked debate on federalism, the tenure of legislatures, premature dissolution of Houses and the basic structure of the Constitution. items.title: CIRP under IBC can continue even if insolvency plea that triggered it was fraudulent: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday held that a corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) can continue even if the insolvency application that originally triggered the process is subsequently found to have been fraudulent and collusive [Orris Vs Rakesh Kumar Gupta]. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe held that while the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) has the power to recall the admission of an insolvency application obtained through fraud, such a finding does not automatically require the entire CIRP to be terminated. “ The initiating creditor is merely the triggering creditor, and not the proprietor of the CIRP, ” the judgment said. Once an insolvency application is admitted, the proceedings cease to remain a dispute between the creditor who initiated the process and the corporate debtor. They become proceedings in rem involving the entire body of creditors and other stakeholders, the Court explained. “ The resolution process can therefore continue even in the absence of the original applicant, ” the top court made it clear. However, the NCLT subsequently found that the insolvency proceedings had been initiated through fraud and collusion between Straight Edge and the corporate debtor. Among other things, it found that two persons who had represented Three C Shelters as directors and admitted the alleged liability were, in fact, described as an office boy and pantry boy who were unaware of the company's affairs. The NCLT also found discrepancies in documents relied upon to establish the purported operational debt. Hence, it set aside the CIRP. The decision was upheld by the NCLAT. This led to the appeal before the Supreme Court. The apex court affirmed the findings of fraud and collusion, observing that the supposed debt was a "mirage" and had been projected to enable initiation of CIRP and the consequent moratorium, thereby blocking remedies available to homebuyers and other claimants. items.summary: The Bombay High Court at Goa on Thursday expressed concern about the manner in which Election Commission of India's (ECI) automated software system rejects form 8 applications filed by electors to report a change of address [Paresh Salgaonkar & Ors v. State of Goa & Ors.] Under the automated system, form 8 applications are rejected if the applicant fails to submit a pre-filled enumeration form at their previous residence. The Court remarked that while the ECI’s protocol successfully purges non-resident entries, it fails to achieve its corresponding goal of enumerating shifted voters. The Bench also noted that rejection orders cited "system glitches," indicating the portal gave officers no choice but to reject form 8 filings. The Court also took exception to the ECI invoking public perception and confidence in the electoral exercise to support the commission's revision framework. The Bench rebuked the ECI and made it clear that court proceedings are governed strictly by legal provisions rather than external opinion and public sentiment should not be a ground to bypass the law. “What the public thinks about all of us is immaterial. We are dealing here in a court,” the judge said. The division bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar was hearing a plea filed by a family of five members in Goa challenging deletion of their names from the electoral rolls and the rejection of their form 8 applications following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit S. items.title: Delhi High Court blocks ₹213 crore payout by SAIL to British company over unstamped arbitral award
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has blocked the release of over ₹213 crore deposited by Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) towards an arbitral award in favour of British Marine PLC after finding that the award was unstamped and could not presently be enforced. [British Marine v. SAIL] Justice Vinod Kumar held that an unstamped arbitral award is not executable and rejected British Marine's application seeking release of the balance amount deposited by SAIL. “ Unstamped Award would not be executable, therefore, the amount cannot be released to Decree Holder ,” the Court said The Court, however, clarified that British Marine could take steps to bring the original arbitral award before the High Court, pay the requisite stamp duty and, thereafter, move a fresh application for release of the money. Delhi HC judge Justice Vinod Kumar The case arose from an arbitral award passed in favour of British Marine, which had initiated enforcement proceedings before the Delhi High Court. SAIL had challenged the award under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. Pursuant to orders passed in December 2023 and February 2024, SAIL deposited ₹230.33 crore with the Registrar General of the High Court, representing 50 per cent of the decretal amount. Of this, ₹17.09 crore was subsequently released to British Marine against a bank guarantee. SAIL's challenge to the arbitral award under Section 34 was dismissed on October 13, 2025. Its appeal under Section 37 was also dismissed by a Division Bench of the High Court on September 17 this year. British Marine then sought release of the remaining ₹213.24 crore lying with the Court. SAIL told the Court that it had filed a special leave petition (SLP) before the Supreme Court, though there was no stay operating against enforcement of the award. It nevertheless opposed the release on the ground that the award itself was unstamped and, therefore, could not be executed The High Court noted that the original arbitral award was not before it. Both sides informed the Court that the original was lying in a sealed cover with the Supreme Court pursuant to directions issued in an earlier round of proceedings in 2022. Justice Kumar observed that while an arbitral award is a chargeable instrument, a copy of the award can neither be stamped nor impounded under the Stamp Act. Since the original was unavailable, the Court said the defect could not presently be cured. The Court consequently dismissed British Marine's application for release

items.title: Rajanna R elected chairperson of Karnataka State Bar Council; Shivamurthy is new vice chairperson
items.summary: Advocate Rajanna R has been elected as the new chairperson of the Karnataka State Bar Council (KSBC) while advocate Shivamurthy has been elected as vice-chairperson. Advocate Dhananjaya CM was elected as the Karnataka State Bar Council's nominee to the Bar Council of India (BCI). They will hold office for two years. The elections to the three posts were held on Wednesday, with the Advocate General of Karnataka, 23 elected members of the KSBC and two co-opted women members participating in the voting. Rajanna secured 15 votes, defeating advocate N Devaraj who secured 11 votes. Shivamurthy secured 17 votes, defeating advocate Shylaja K who polled 9 votes. The KSBC elections were held on March 11 for the constitution of the 23-member council. As many as 149 candidates had contested the election. A notable feature of the 2026 KSBC election was the election of five women advocates to the 23-member council, marking the first time that five women members have been elected to the State Bar Council. The KSBC election had been pending for several years, with the previous election having been held about eight years earlier. The delay was connected with issues concerning the Certificate of Practice (CoP) and the process for determining eligible voters. The Supreme Court had directed that the KSBC election be conducted before March 15 The elections were then held on March 11. Following the constitution of the new council, the election of its chairperson, vice-chairperson and BCI nominee was conducted by the members of the council on Wednesday (September 30). items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Thursday asked the Punjab government to expedite the process of appointing a regular Director General of Police (DGP) in the State [ Nikhil Thamman v State of Punjab & Ors ]. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor passed the order on a petition filed by advocate Nikhil Thamman who said that the State has been without a regular head of police force since 2022. Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor The plea before the Court stated that in accordance with Supreme Court directions, the DGP is required to be selected by the State government from amongst the three senior-most officers empanelled for promotion to that rank by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) based on their length of service, very good record and range of experience for heading the police force. A minimum tenure of two years was intended to bring stability and continuity to the police leadership and reduce arbitrary and frequent changes to the highest office, the petitioner argued. However, the plea added that Punjab has had an additional-charge arrangement for the post of head of police force since DGP Gaurav Yadav was given the charge, in addition to his duties as Special DGP, Administration, Punjab. Thamman also told the Court that the State government had already received a panel of officers for the selection of the DGP but no action was towards making a regular appointment. An affidavit filed before the High Court by the State revealed that the panel is under active consideration of the government. Considering the same, the Court directed the State to comply with the Supreme Court mandate and file a compliance affidavit by October 13. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday upheld the validity of the law allowing elderly parents or senior citizens to apply to a District Magistrate (DM) to evict their children or legal heirs from the property belonging to the parents [Punam v Divisional Commissioner, GNCT Of Delhi & Ors] . A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said that Rule 22(3)(1) of the Delhi Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Rules, 2009, provides relief to a senior citizen/parent to mitigate his/her sufferings on account of non-maintenance and ill-treatment. It held that the provision derives its existence from Sections 22 and 32 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 (Senior Citizens Act) and cannot be declared ultra vires. While Section 22 empowers the State government to prescribe measures for protecting the life and property of senior citizens, Section 32 grants it the rule-making power. “In view of the aforesaid discussion, the challenge laid by the petitioner on the provisions of Rule 22 (3)(1)(i) and (iv) of the 2009 Rules fails, which is hereby rejected,” the Bench concluded. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia Delhi High Court Rule 22 (3)(1)(i) of the 2009 Rules provides relief to a senior citizen/parents to mitigate his/her sufferings on account of non-maintenance and ill-treatment. The High Court rendered the findings while dismissing a plea filed by one Punam. She had challenged an eviction order passed by the Divisional Commissioner of Delhi in favour of her mother-in-law. Punam had argued that the Senior Citizens Act does not expressly provide for eviction proceedings and that the rules exceeded the State government's rule-making powers. She stated that she had married the senior citizen's son in 1996, and the couple had two children. items.title: Child custody cases: Karnataka High Court suggests replacing 'visitation' with 'parenting time'
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday expressed the need for change in the terminology employed in judicial proceedings that concern child custody. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti questioned how a trial court had passed an order that allowed the father to visit the child on weekends for 3-4 hours, 50% of school vacations and 30 minutes of call time on WhatsApp between 7:30 to 8:30 PM. Justice Kanneganti also said that courts must replace the phrase 'visitation time' with 'parenting time'. "Courts often use the word "visitation" to describe the time the child spends with a parent who is a non-custodial parent. The term is familiar, but it carries an unfortunate suggestion that one parent is part of the child's life while the other merely visits. A child should not be made to understand the relationship through the word "visitation," which is used for someone who arrives and leaves as a guest. Children read the conduct of adults and sometimes the words of Courts to understand where they belong. Calling it parenting time recognizes a simple truth that no parent is a visitor in the life of a child." Justice Lalitha kanneganti The Court further appealed to advocates in custody cases to cooperate in such cases. "The same aggression that we see in the parties, let it not be in the advocates, lets all together resolve their problems. Let's not create further problems with them." The couple had separated since 2017 and the 9-year-old child was in the custody of the mother. The father had last seen the child when he was 3 months old. A family court had granted divorce and an order in favour of the wife in a domestic violence case. Under these circumstances, a trial court had allowed the father to meet the child on weekends between 11:00 AM to 7:00 PM, 50% of the summer, winter, Dasara, Deepavali vacations and calls between 7:30 PM to 8:30 PM on alternate days. The mother had approached the High Court to quash the order passed by the trial court. The Court appreciated the trial court having followed a joint parenting plan directed by the Karnataka High Court. However, it said that the plan was to be applied after weighing the facts and circumstances of every individual case. "This approach of the Courts is not in the interest of the child. Particularly, in family disputes and child custody matters, there cannot be any straitjacket formula. As the Courts are dealing with the emotions, lives of parents and children, it all depends upon the facts and circumstances of each case

items.title: Five FIRs filed across Karnataka over alleged misuse of Form 7, BJP threatens protest
items.summary: Five FIRs have been registered across Karnataka over alleged attempts to delete voters from electoral rolls through bulk Form 7 applications during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). These FIRs have been filed in the wake of strong objection to the use of Form 7 to allegedly disenfranchise Muslims on a mass scale. The FIRs have been registered in Belagavi, Bidar and Mysuru districts following complaints alleging the use of false information, forged documents and applications submitted without the knowledge of voters. The cases have been filed under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to cheating, forgery, impersonation and criminal conspiracy. Chief Electoral Officer for Karnataka V Anbu Kumar said in a press release that although 84,900 Form 7s had been received, the ECI had not taken anyone off the electoral rolls. He also said ECI officials had been directed to take action against those who had “knowingly made false claims” while filing Form 6, Form 6A, Form 7, and Form 8, under Section 31 of the Representation of People’s Act after conducting inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules. The complaint alleges that Form 7 applications seeking deletion of 198 voters were prepared and submitted to Booth Level Officers as genuine documents issued by the Electoral Registration Officer. Sanadi said he found his own name, along with the names of his brother, relatives and neighbours, among hundreds of applications at Veerabhadra Urdu Model School in Belagavi. For at least 15 years, Sanadi has been the BLA at polling station 196, where he is also the chairman of the school. BLOs at the polling stations told The Hindu that two men claiming to be from the Belagavi City Corporation brought bulk Form 7 applications seeking deletion of Muslim voters. items.title: ‘No present or ongoing system of Devadasi dedication’: Karnataka tells SC
items.summary: The Karnataka government, on Thursday, October 1, told the Supreme Court that the practice of dedicating women or girls as Devadasis is not currently prevalent in any of the 15 districts where it was historically reported, following a district-level verification exercise by state authorities. A bench of Justices Augustine George Masih and R Mahadevan took note of the state’s affidavit and directed Karnataka to provide further details on rehabilitation and awareness measures for former Devadasis. The court listed the matter for the next hearing after four weeks. The 15 districts covered by the verification are Bellary, Koppal, Yadgir, Kalaburagi, Davangere, Haveri, Vijayanagara, Dharwad, Shivamogga, Vijayapura, Belagavi, Raichur, Gadag, Chitradurga, and Bagalkot. According to Live Law , the state said that inquiries were conducted by the Women and Child Development Department and the Karnataka State Women Development Corporation through Devadasi Dedication Prohibition Officers and police authorities. “On the basis of the information and reports received from the concerned Devadasi Dedication Prohibition Officers in consultation with the police department, the state respectfully submits that the Devadasi system, in the sense of dedication of women or girls as Devadasis, is not presently in practice in any of the 15 districts,” the affidavit stated. The state, however, acknowledged that former Devadasis continue to live in these districts and said measures were necessary to ensure that the practice is not revived. The affidavit was submitted to the court by Vasanthi Uppar, General Manager of the Karnataka State Women Development Corporation. The state counsel told the court that multi-level inquiries through Devadasi Dedication Prohibition Officers and police authorities across all 15 districts had found no ongoing system of dedication. The state also informed the court that 33 cases have been registered since the Karnataka Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1982 came into force, with 12 resulting in convictions. The remaining cases are at various stages of inquiry and hearing. The state said that the presence of former Devadasis in the districts does not by itself establish that the dedication system continues. items.title: Over 2 lakh Telangana voters received SIR notices without reason cited: Study
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. More than two lakh voters in Telangana have received notices as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls with no mention of what discrepancy prompted the action. According to an analysis of election data by the Sabar Institute and the Constitutional Guardians Forum, 2.01 lakh electors (2,01,249) were issued notices with the “reason for discrepancy” field left blank. The analysis examined 92.85 lakh discrepancy notices, which make up 31.3% of the state’s electorate. The largest category was voters classified as ‘unmapped with last SIR’, accounting for 32.37 lakh (34.9%) notices. Another 25.97 lakh (28%) notices related to a mismatch in the parent’s name. Self-name mismatches accounted for 11.14 lakh notices. The notices issued were particularly high in constituencies bordering Hyderabad. Quthbullapur recorded notices for 66.6% of its electorate, followed by Kukatpally at 65.4%, Uppal at 57%, Medchal at 56%, and Serilingampally at 55.8%. The study also examined the religious composition of voters named in the notices. Overall, Muslim electors accounted for 14.16% of the notices, or 13.14 lakh cases. Their share was substantially higher in several Hyderabad constituencies, including Bahadurpura, Chandrayangutta, Karwan, and Yakutpura. In Bahadurpura, Muslim names accounted for 85.18% of the notices, while the corresponding figures were 71.15% in Chandrayangutta, 54.56% in Karwan, and 61.16% in Yakutpura. The analysis found that the reasons recorded in the notices varied considerably. Apart from unmapped voters and parent-name mismatches, other categories included self-name mismatches, parent-child age differences, and gaps of less than nine months between siblings. Notices were also issued in cases involving six or more children — Muslim names accounted for 50.5% of the notices in this category, according to the study.

items.title: Jr NTR, Janhvi Kapoor condemn vulgar AI video of Chuttamalle song, vow legal action
items.summary: After a sexually explicit, AI-generated video of the popular Telugu song “Chuttamalle” from Devara: Part 1 surfaced on the internet, actors Jr NTR and Janhvi Kapoor came out in condemnation, calling it “disgusting” and “disturbing”. Released in September 2024, the film stars Jr NTR and Janhvi Kapoor in lead roles. “Chuttamalle”, a romantic number composed by Anirudh Ravichander and sung by Shilpa Rao, became popular when it was released. The new AI video manipulates Janhvi’s appearance to make it sexually explicit and vulgar, raising alarm about the misuse of AI to objectify women. “In a land that worships women as mothers and goddesses, where "Matrudevo Bhava" is not just a phrase but a part of our culture, some people have fallen so low that they are using AI to disrespect a woman in the most degrading way possible. Using AI to create something this vile is shameful beyond words,” Jr NTR wrote on social media platform X. Urging netizens not to engage with the video or share it, the actor also vowed to take legal action against those behind it. “To the scumbags behind this morphed ‘Chuttamalle’ video, I will not spare any of you. I will take every possible legal action against those who created it and those who are spreading it. Please do not watch, share or engage with such content. Today it is someone else. Tomorrow, it could be your mother, sister, wife, or daughter. This is a serious issue, and I urge all the state governments and the Government of India to act strongly and bring in strict regulations against the misuse of AI,” he further wrote. Janhvi also posted on X, citing this as a “clear misuse of AI”. “It’s disturbing to see AI-generated fake videos being circulated. Please don’t create, share, or promote such content. This is a clear misuse of AI. Legal action will definitely be taken against those involved,” she wrote. This is not the first time that AI has been used to generate fake, explicit videos of women actors. Previously, actors Rukmini Vasanth, Shalini Pandey, Alia Bhatt, and Rashmika Mandanna, among others, have spoken against such practices, urging tighter legal scrutiny.

items.title: TVK complains to ECI against MK Stalin for body-shaming comment on P Sathyabama
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) has approached the Election Commission of India (ECI), seeking action against the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) president MK Stalin for allegedly violating the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) by making derogatory remarks about the physical appearance of the party's Dharapuram by-poll candidate, P Sathyabama. Addressing a representation to the state’s Chief Electoral Officer on October 3, Minister and the party's election campaign management general secretary Aadhav Arjuna has sought the cancellation of Stalin's star campaigner status and urged the ECI to direct the District Returning Officer to register a First Information Report (FIR) against him under Section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women. Aadhav also sought restrictions on Stalin's election campaign, including preventing him from addressing public rallies and giving interviews for a specified period. The complaint was filed following Stalin's campaign speech in Dharapuram on Friday, October 2, in which he referred to Sathyabama as 'Petti Bama' (Suitcase Bama) and 'Palti Bama' (Somersault Bama), before remarking on her physical appearance. Addressing a public meeting in the constituency, Stalin asked the gathering what they called the TVK candidate. "You, the people, what do you call her now? Petti Bama. There's another one too, Palti Bama. I don't know how she managed to somersault with that kind of appearance," he said. The term 'Petti Bama' has been used by the DMK during its campaign to allege that Sathyabama switched parties after being offered money. Sathyabama has denied the allegation. The complaint said that such remarks were intended to discourage women from participating in public life. The party also alleged that similar remarks against women had become a recurring practice within the DMK, particularly by Stalin and his son Udhayanidhi Stalin. In a statement, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay also accused the DMK of organising a campaign meeting that was defamatory and indecent in nature. "As a son, elder brother and younger brother of the women of Tamil Nadu, I strongly condemn the evil force, the DMK, for repeatedly speaking obscenely about women," Vijay said. தாராபுரம் தொகுதி இடைத்தேர்தல் பரப்புரைப் பொதுக்கூட்டம் என்ற பெயரில், தீய சக்தியான தி.மு.க. சார்பில் ஓர் அவதூறு மற்றும் அநாகரிகக் கூட்டத்தை நடத்தியுள்ளார், அதன் தலைவர் திரு. மு.க.ஸ்டாலின் அவர்கள். நமது தாராபு

items.title: R Sreelekha’s resignation bid puts ruling BJP in trouble at Tvm Corporation
items.summary: Putting the Bharatiya Janata Party-ruled Thiruvananthapuram Corporation in deep trouble, councillor and former Director General of Police R Sreelekha has submitted her resignation letter to Mayor V V Rajesh, citing personal reasons. The resignation, however, has not been official yet as the letter has to be ideally submitted to the Corporation secretary as per the Kerala Municipality Act (KMA). The resignation move is a major setback to the BJP, which has been ruling the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation with a razor-thin majority. The BJP currently rules the 101-member Corporation with 50 councillors, backed by an independent councillor. If the resignation is accepted, the number of BJP councillors will drop to 49. As per reports, Sreelekha submitted the resignation letter to the Mayor on September 30. However, the incident came out only on Saturday, October 3, when the retired Indian Police Service (IPS) officer announced it in a WhatsApp group related to her ward. In the message, Sreelekha added that she would submit the resignation letter to the district collector on Monday. Later, Mayor Rajesh confirmed to the media that he received a letter, where Sreelekha has cited some personal inconvenience to continue the councillor post. He, however, added that it could be considered as a resignation letter only if submitted to the Corporation Secretary. Corporation Secretary J Mohammed Shafi told the media that he has not received any letter from the councillor. As per section 40 of the KMA, councillors should submit their resignation letter in prescribed form to the secretary. The secretary will then notify the state election commission and the council about the vacancy. Sreelekha has not responded to the media yet. In the past, Sreelekha had openly expressed her displeasure after BJP chose Rajesh over her for the post of Mayor. Sreelekha who was the BJP vice president was reluctant to contest for the 2025 local body election and was reportedly convinced only after senior BJP leaders offered her the post of Mayor. Later, the post was given to Rajesh, allegedly due to the intervention of senior functionaries of Rashitriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). Sreelekha’s abstention during the swearing in ceremony of the Mayor was particularly noticed. Though Sreelekha attempted to contest the Assembly election from Shastamangalam in 2026, she was pushed to the third position in a tight contest between Congress’ K Muraleedharan and Communist Party of India (Marxist)’s V K Pras

items.title: Andhra: Five killed, 10 injured in boiler blast at pharma unit in Tirupati’s Sri City
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. At least five workers were killed and more than 10 others injured after a boiler exploded at the TIL Healthcare Private Limited, a pharmaceutical company located in Sri City Special Economic Zone (SEZ), in Tirupati district. The incident occurred at around 8 am on Saturday, October 3 when workers were engaged in the morning shift at the manufacturing unit. An explosion triggered a fire, leaving several workers injured. The injured were rushed to a hospital within the Sri City premises for treatment. While initial reports put the death toll at four, Tirupati Superintendent of Police (SP) L Subbarayudu later confirmed that five people had died. Two workers died at the spot, while others succumbed to their injuries during treatment. Three victims have been identified as Gourab Roy (35), Chinna Mastan (36) and Ramesh (40). Vasu (36), who was critically injured in the blast, died while undergoing treatment at a hospital in Chennai, reports said. The exact number of workers present at the facility when the explosion occurred is yet to be established. Officials are also investigating the cause of the blast, including the possibility of a technical fault in the boiler. Rescue and relief operations were launched immediately after the incident, while authorities began collecting details about the workers affected. Expressing grief over the incident, Andhra Pradesh IT and HRD Minister Nara Lokesh described the explosion as a tragic accident and directed officials to ensure that those injured receive the best possible medical care.
